129	
130	## Scale
131	
132	At 100 % a video or picture draws at its native pixels, one source pixel to one canvas pixel, so a 1920 × 1080 clip on a 3840 × 2160 canvas covers a quarter of it. The field shows one decimal place.
133	
134	A new clip bigger than the canvas doesn't start at 100 %. **Fit new clips to canvas** on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) is on unless you change it, and while it's on the clip starts at the scale that fits.
135	
136	Scale pivots on the centre of the uncropped picture. It works on every clip that draws, text, shapes and graphics included.
137	
138	## Position
139	
140	Position places the clip's centre in canvas pixels, measured from the centre of the canvas. At 0, 0 the clip sits in the middle. **Position X** runs right and **Position Y** runs down, so negative values go left and up.
141	
142	Both are typed fields, shown in whole pixels, with no slider. To place a clip by eye, drag it on the canvas. On a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip the fields still measure the centre of the uncropped picture.
143	
144	## Rotation
145	
146	Rotation turns the clip about its centre, and a positive angle turns it clockwise on screen. The field shows one decimal place, and the rotation grip on the canvas sets the same value by hand.
147	
148	## Opacity
149	
150	Opacity sets how see-through the clip is: at 100 % it's solid, and at 0 % it's fully transparent.
151	
152	## Fit and fill
153	
154	Both buttons scale each selected clip and centre it, setting its position to 0, 0.
155	
156	- **Fit to Canvas** makes the whole picture fit inside the canvas, so you may see the background at two edges.
157	- **Fill Canvas** makes the picture cover the whole canvas, so its edges may run off two sides.
158	
159	Each clip gets its own scale from its own size, and all of them together are one undo step. A shape uses its box, a graphic its size and a nest its own canvas.
160	
161	Good to know:
162	
163	- Text clips are skipped, because their size comes from the words. So is any clip with no known size. If that leaves nothing to scale, Frame Job beeps.
164	- Both buttons measure the uncropped picture, so a [cropped](/canvas/crop/) clip can leave a gap after **Fill Canvas**.
165	- Rotation stays as it is and isn't counted, so a rotated clip may not fit or fill the way it would upright.
166	- A scale past the 1 to 1000 % range isn't applied, so a very small picture on a large canvas can get an error from **Fill Canvas** instead.
167	
168	## Reset
169	
170	**Reset** in the section's header puts position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend and motion blur back to their defaults in one step. It shows only while the section differs from its default.
171	
172	It leaves the [crop](/canvas/crop/) alone, which has its own **Reset**. To put back a single row, right-click its label and choose **Reset to default**.
173	
174	## Animate these values
175	
176	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, Scale, Position, Rotation, Opacity and Motion Blur set the action's end state, and the clip ramps there along the action's curve. Blend switches at the action's end instead. **Reset** is hidden while you edit an action. **Clear** appears there once the action changes one of these rows, and takes the section out of the action.
177	
178	See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
179	
180	## No stretching
181	
182	Scale is uniform for pictures. A video, image or nest always keeps its proportions, and there's no separate width and height. **Scale** and the canvas handles keep a graphic's proportions too.
183	
184	Three kinds of clip can change on one axis: a shape, through its box's width and height, text, through its wrap width, and a graphic, through **Width** and **Height** in its Size section, which draw it at the new size rather than stretching it. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/), [Text box and wrapping](/text-and-shapes/text-box/) and [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height).
185	
186	## With an agent
187	
188	`set_video` sets these with `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity` and `blend`. Some of its numbers differ from the inspector's:
189	
190	| Key | Takes |
191	| --- | --- |
192	| `scale` | 0.01 to 10, where 1 is native pixels, the inspector's 100 % |
193	| `opacity` | 0 to 1 |
194	| `x`, `y`, `rotation` | Any finite number, with no limit like the inspector's |
195	
196	A value outside its range gets an error rather than being pulled back into the range. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend).
197	
198	## Related
199	
200	- [Move, scale and rotate](/canvas/move-scale-rotate/)
201	- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
202	- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
203	- [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/)
204	---
205	title: Blend modes
206	description: Choose how a layer combines with what's under it, and understand why a blend can look like it isn't working.
207	---
208	
209	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
210	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
211	
212	A blend mode decides how a layer's colours combine with whatever is already on the canvas under it. Use one to lay a glow over a shot, darken with a texture, or mix two pictures.
213	
214	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Transform ▸ Blend" tools="set_video" />
215	
216	## The Blend popup
217	
218	<Steps>
219	
220	1. Put the layer you want to blend on a track in front of something to blend with.
221	
222	2. Select it and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).
223	
224	3. In **Transform**, choose a mode from the **Blend** popup.
225	
226	</Steps>
227	
228	Every clip starts on **Normal**. The change is one undo step, and with several clips selected it applies to all of them.
229	
230	Hover over the popup for a reminder of what a blend needs behind it.
231	
232	## The eight modes
233	
234	These are in the popup's order. "Underneath" means every layer behind this one, and the canvas background.
235	
236	| Mode | What it does |
237	| --- | --- |
238	| **Normal** | Draws over what's underneath. |
239	| **Multiply** | Darkens, by multiplying with what's underneath. |
240	| **Screen** | Lightens, the inverse of Multiply. A screened white blob reads as a glow. |
241	| **Add** | Adds the colours together. |
242	| **Overlay** | Multiplies where what's underneath is dark, and screens where it's light. |
243	| **Darken** | Keeps the darker of the two colours. |
244	| **Lighten** | Keeps the lighter of the two colours. |
245	| **Difference** | Gives the absolute difference of the two colours. |
246	
247	## Nothing behind
248	
249	A blend needs something under the layer, and over the empty black canvas it can't do much:
250	
251	| Mode | Over the empty black canvas |
252	| --- | --- |
253	| **Multiply**, **Darken**, **Overlay** | The layer reads black. |
254	| **Screen**, **Add**, **Lighten**, **Difference** | The layer looks unchanged. |
255	
256	The Transform section warns you when that's what's happening, for example "Nothing behind this clip — multiply reads black here." or "Nothing behind this clip — add changes nothing here."
257	
258	The note looks at the clip's whole span, not only the frame at the playhead, so it stays away if anything sits behind any part of the clip. Hidden tracks don't count, and neither do clips with their picture turned off. With several clips selected, it's about the first one.
259	
260	It appears only while the canvas background is opaque black. Over a transparent canvas, a blend draws the layer untouched.
261	
262	To give the layer something to blend against:
263	
264	- Use **Clip ▸ Add Background** to put a plate on a new track at the back. See [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/).
265	- Set a non-black **Background** on the Document tab. See [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
266	
267	## During a transition
268	
269	A layer always draws as **Normal** for as long as it's in a [transition](/motion/transitions/), whatever blend mode it has. The popup keeps showing the clip's own mode during the overlap. Only the frames in the overlap draw as Normal.
270	
271	## Animate a blend mode
272	
273	An [action](/motion/actions/) can change the mode. It doesn't ramp from one to the other: it holds, then switches at the action's end, and the row shows `at end` while you're editing that action.
274	
275	## Good to know
276	
277	- **Nest clips.** The popup is greyed on a nest clip, with the note "A nest has no pixels of its own to blend — un-group it (⇧⌘G) to blend the clips inside." Use **Clip ▸ Un-nest**, blend the clip you wanted, and nest again.
278	- **Clips inside a nest.** You can blend a clip inside a nest. It blends against the canvas below the whole nest, not against the nest's own clips under it.
279	- **Adjustment clips.** An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) takes no blend mode.
280	- **Matte tracks.** A clip on a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) keeps its blend mode, but it has no effect while the track is a matte.
281	- **Encoded or linear light.** A project can blend in either. See [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/).
282	
283	## With an agent
284	
285	`set_video` sets the mode with `blend`, one of `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten` or `difference`. Any mode but `normal` on a nest clip gets the error "clip 7 shows a nest and cannot take a blend mode". See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend).
286	
287	## Related
288	
289	- [Position, scale, rotation and opacity](/canvas/transform/)
290	- [Backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/)
291	- [Blending: encoded or linear light](/hdr/blending/)
292	- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)

294	title: Corner radius
295	description: Round the corners of a video clip, image clip or freeze frame, from a soft edge to a pill or a circle.
296	---
297	
298	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
299	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
300	
301	Corner radius rounds the corners of a picture, which is handy for a picture-in-picture or a screen recording sitting on a background.
302	
303	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Corner Radius ▸ Radius" tools="set_video" />
304	
305	## Round the corners
306	
307	<Steps>
308	
309	1. Select a video clip, image clip or freeze frame and open the [Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/).
310	
311	2. Open the **Corner Radius** section.
312	
313	3. Drag **Radius**, type a value, or click the chevron for a [quick pick](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#use-a-quick-pick).
314	
315	</Steps>
316	
317	| Row | What it does | Default | Range | Quick picks |
318	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
319	| **Radius** | How round the corners are, in source pixels | 0 px | 0 to 500 px | 0, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 |
320	
321	Each change is one undo step. Closed, the section's summary reads the radius, such as `32 px`. **Reset** appears in its header while the radius isn't 0.
322	
323	## How the radius is measured
324	
325	The radius is in the source's own pixels, so it scales with the clip. A radius of 32 px on a clip at 50 % looks like 16 px on the canvas.
326	
327	It rounds the [cropped](/canvas/crop/) picture, so the curve follows the crop rather than the original frame. A [shadow](/effects/shadow/) follows the rounded shape.
328	
329	A radius can't be more than half the picture's shorter side, and anything above that draws as that half. So a big enough radius turns a wide picture into a pill and a square picture into a circle. **Radius** stops at 500 px, so it gets there only when the picture's shorter side, after any crop, is 1,000 px or less.
330	
331	## Animate the radius
332	
333	With an [action](/motion/actions/) selected, **Radius** sets the action's end state, and the corners ramp there along the action's curve. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
334	
335	## Good to know
336	
337	Only video clips, image clips and freeze frames have this section. A rectangle shape has its own radius: see [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/).
338	
339	## With an agent
340	
341	`set_video` sets this with `corner_radius`, in source pixels. It takes any value of 0 or more, without the inspector's 500 px stop. See [Tools: picture and grade](/mcp/tools-set-video/#crop-and-corners).
342	
343	## Related
344	
345	- [Crop](/canvas/crop/)
346	- [Shadow](/effects/shadow/)
347	- [The Picture tab](/canvas/picture-tab/)

349	title: Backgrounds
350	description: Fill the space around your footage with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip, on a new track behind everything.
351	---
352	
353	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
354	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
355	
356	A screen recording that doesn't fill the frame, a phone clip on a landscape canvas or a title standing on nothing all leave the canvas showing. A background fills that space with a colour, a picture or a blurred copy of the clip itself.
357	
358	To change the colour of the canvas itself, see [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
359	
360	<AtAGlance
361	  menu={[
362	    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color',
363	    'Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…',
364	    'Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background',
365	  ]}
366	  tools={['add_background', 'add_blurred_background']}
367	/>
368	
369	## Solid Color
370	
371	Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Solid Color**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.
372	
373	Frame Job adds a canvas-sized white rectangle named "Background", starting at 0 and as long as the timeline. It's white because the canvas is black by default, and a black background would seem to do nothing.
374	
375	Recolour it in the **Fill** row of the **Shape** sub-tab, or turn on **Gradient** there for a full-canvas ramp. See [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/) and [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/).
376	
377	## Image
378	
379	<Steps>
380	
381	1. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Background ▸ Image…**. You don't need a selection, and there's no key for it.
382	
383	2. Pick a picture. The panel offers any image type macOS can read, and only image files.
384	
385	</Steps>
386	
387	The picture goes behind everything, scaled to fill the canvas and as long as the timeline. It's named "Background". Fill means it covers the whole canvas and any overflow is cut off at the edges, whatever [**Fit new clips to canvas**](/projects/background-and-timecode/#fit-new-clips-to-canvas) says. To see the whole picture instead, scale it down afterwards.
388	
389	The picture joins the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) in the same undo step. If it's already there, the existing entry is reused.
390	
391	If the file can't be read, an alert says so and nothing is added. "Could Not Add the Picture" means it couldn't join the project's media list.
392	
393	## Blurred background
394	
395	This is the usual backdrop for a screen recording or a vertical video: the clip's own picture, blown up past the frame and blurred, so the colours always match.
396	
397	<Steps>
398	
399	1. Select one clip.
400	
401	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Blurred Background**. There's no key for it.
402	
403	</Steps>
404	
405	Frame Job puts a copy behind everything, named "Blurred Background", and selects the copy rather than the original, so you can adjust its blur or its scale straight away. The copy is:
406	
407	- at the same start and length, with the same speed and the same part of the source, so both play the same frames
408	- scaled to fill the canvas, centred and uncropped
409	- blended **Normal**, whatever the original uses
410	- blurred by one full-strength Blur [filter](/effects/filters/), which replaces any filters on the original
411	- muted, so the sound doesn't play twice
412	
413	The command works on video, image, freeze frame, shape and graphic clips. It's greyed for a text clip, an adjustment clip and a clip of an audio-only file, which have no picture size to scale to the canvas. It's also greyed for a nest clip, because a blurred copy of a nest would come out sharp, and when you've selected no clips or more than one.
414	
415	## What a blurred background follows
416	
417	The copy matches the clip at the moment you add it. After that it's a separate clip: moving or trimming the original doesn't move or trim the copy.
418	
419	| The copy leaves behind | So |
420	| --- | --- |
421	| Transition | It's alone on its track, with nothing to transition from. |
422	| Actions | A zoom on the foreground doesn't zoom the backdrop. A speed ramp is an action too, so a copy of a ramped clip plays at the clip's steady speed and doesn't stay in step with it. |
423	| Motion presets and Motion Blur | The backdrop doesn't slide, spin or pulse with the clip in front. |
424	| Remove Background and Behind Subject | The backdrop stays whole. |
425	| Label and ducking | The label isn't copied, and the copy doesn't lower the rest of the mix. |
426	
427	Every other picture setting carries over, including opacity, rotation, corner radius, the colour controls, the drop shadow and the reflection. A rotated clip gives a rotated backdrop, and the fill is worked out as if the picture were square to the canvas, so a large rotation can leave the corners showing.
428	
429	The copy's picture is always on, even if the original's is [turned off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
430	
431	## A new back-most track
432	
433	Each of the three commands puts one clip on a new track behind every other track, and selects it. A new track is the only place that's sure to be behind everything, with no overlap to check.
434	
435	The track gets the next numbered name, such as "Track 4". One undo step takes the clip and the track away again. The steps are called **Add Background** and **Add Blurred Background**.
436	
437	## Good to know
438	
439	- A colour or picture background is as long as the timeline when you add it, and it doesn't grow with the timeline. Drag its end to [trim](/editing/trimming/) it longer.
440	- On an empty timeline, a colour or picture background is one frame long.
441	- Fill stops at a scale of 1000%, so a picture less than a tenth of the canvas's width or height can't reach the edges.
442	- With a nest open, a background goes on the nest's own tracks, behind everything inside the nest.
443	- A project holds up to 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and Frame Job won't add a background past that.
444	
445	## With an agent
446	
447	`add_background` with no arguments adds the white background, and `add_blurred_background` takes the `clip` to copy.
448	
449	An agent can do two things the menu can't. It can give the background a `color` and a `duration` of its own, at least one frame long, and it can pass the `media` of a movie that's already in the project instead of a picture. It can't pass `media` and `color` together, and a file with no picture, such as a LUT, can't be a background.
450	
451	A movie background keeps its sound and stops where its file ends, so only a picture or a colour runs the whole timeline. See [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_background).
452	
453	## Related
454	
455	- [Canvas background and timecode](/projects/background-and-timecode/)
456	- [Shape fill, stroke and size](/text-and-shapes/shape-settings/)
457	- [Gradient fills](/text-and-shapes/gradients/)
458	- [Filters](/effects/filters/)
459	- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
460	- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)

462	title: Matte tracks
463	description: Make one track cut the track behind it, so text, a shape or a movie becomes a window onto your footage.
464	---
465	
466	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
467	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
468	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
469	
470	A matte track cuts the track directly behind it. Its own clips are never drawn. Instead, what they show decides where the track behind can be seen, which turns a title or a shape into a window onto your footage.
471	
472	<AtAGlance
473	  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
474	  where="Right-click a track's header or the empty part of its lane ▸ Matte"
475	  tools={['set_track', 'add_adjustment_clip']}
476	/>
477	
478	<Shot
479	  name="10c-matte-track.window"
480	  alt="The editor with three tracks. The Window track carries a Matte · Alpha tag and its rectangle clip is drawn pale with a bracket joining it to the Video track below, so the preview shows the video only inside the rectangle, on a black canvas. The Stray track in front reads Matte · nothing behind. The inspector's Picture sub-tab opens with the note: Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect."
481	/>
482	
483	## What a matte does
484	
485	Any clip that draws can be a matte: text, a shape, a graphic, an image, a movie or a nest.
486	
487	A matte belongs to the track, not the clip. Move a clip off the track and it's an ordinary clip again, and move one on and it becomes part of the matte.
488	
489	Only the track directly behind is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. Adding, moving or removing a track can change which track that is.
490	
491	The cut applies to everything the clip behind draws. Its drop shadow follows the shape that's left, and its reflection is cut where it lands. It all works in the preview, in rendered frames, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.
492	
493	## Setting a matte
494	
495	<Steps>
496	
497	1. Put the clips that will do the cutting, such as a text clip, on the track directly in front of the track you want to cut. On the timeline, that's the track directly above it.
498	
499	2. Select one of those clips, or right-click that track's header.
500	
501	3. Choose a mode from **Track ▸ Matte**, or from the **Matte** submenu of the track's context menu.
502	
503	</Steps>
504	
505	**Track ▸ Matte** works on the track holding the first selected clip, or the front-most track when nothing is selected. The context menu works on the track you clicked. Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click its header or the empty part of its lane to open it.
506	
507	A checkmark shows the track's mode. Choosing the mode it already has beeps and makes no undo step. There's no key for a matte, and the undo step is called **Track Matte**.
508	
509	## The modes
510	
511	| Mode | The track behind shows where the matte clip is |
512	| --- | --- |
513	| **Off** | Not a matte. This is an ordinary track, and every track's default. |
514	| **Alpha** | Opaque |
515	| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
516	| **Luma** | Bright |
517	| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |
518	
519	Brightness is Rec. 709 luma, and transparent counts as black, so a half-transparent white counts as half bright.
520	
521	Everything outside a matte clip's box is transparent. So at any moment a matte clip is playing, **Alpha** and **Luma** hide the track behind outside the clip, and **Inverted Alpha** and **Inverted Luma** show it there.
522	
523	For text, a shape or anything else with see-through parts, start with **Alpha**. A movie or a photo usually fills its box, so **Alpha** would only give you a rectangle. Use **Luma** for those, so their light and dark areas do the cutting.
524	
525	## Gaps
526	
527	Where the matte track has no clip, the track behind shows uncut, whatever the mode.
528	
529	A matte is read moment by moment and no clip is tied to another, so splitting, moving, deleting or pasting can't break a link between them.
530	
531	## Turning a matte off
532	
533	To turn a cut off for a while, use [**Hide Video**](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) on the matte track, or [turn off a matte clip's picture](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/). Either way the track behind shows whole, as it does in a gap. To end the matte for good, choose **Off**.
534	
535	## Nothing to cut
536	
537	A matte with no target cuts nothing, and its clips still draw nothing. That happens on the back-most track, and on a track directly in front of another matte track. So two matte tracks in a row don't combine: only the one nearest the track behind cuts anything.
538	
539	## Matte properties
540	
541	A matte clip is drawn like any other clip, into the matte instead of onto the canvas, so most of its settings shape the cut:
542	
543	- position, scale, rotation and crop
544	- corner radius and opacity
545	- colour, chroma key and filters
546	- spotlight and obscured regions
547	- motion presets and actions
548	- transitions between two matte clips
549	
550	Animate the clip and the cut moves with it, so a moving title can wipe footage on.
551	
552	A matte clip's blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect. They're kept, and apply again when the track stops being a matte.
553	
554	**Motion Blur** has no effect either, on a matte clip or on a clip a matte is cutting. Both draw sharp.
555	
556	A matte clip isn't drawn, but it's still there on the canvas. Click inside its box to select it, and drag it like any clip.
557	
558	## Sound
559	
560	A matte clip's sound still plays. A matte only changes the picture, so **Mute Audio** silences the track as it would any other, and **Hide Video** doesn't.
561	
562	## Adjustment clips
563	
564	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) on a track cut by a matte grades only inside the matte. This is how you confine a grade to one area: put the adjustment clip on a track, and make the track directly in front of it a matte.
565	
566	An adjustment clip on a matte track does nothing, and the Clip tab says so. Its settings are kept.
567	
568	## The note on the Clip tab
569	
570	When every selected clip is on a matte track and those tracks share one mode, every sub-tab of the **Clip** tab shows a note under its strip. Every control stays live, and its value comes back into play when the track stops being a matte.
571	
572	| Selection | Note |
573	| --- | --- |
574	| Clips on a matte track that has a track to cut | "Matte for the track below (Alpha). Not drawn: its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection have no effect." The note names the track's mode. |
575	| Clips on a matte track with nothing to cut | "Nothing is behind this matte track, so it cuts nothing." |
576	| Only adjustment clips, on matte tracks of any mode | "An adjustment clip on a matte track has no effect." |
577	
578	## On the timeline
579	
580	A matte track's header carries a tag such as "Matte · Alpha", under the track name. With nothing to cut, the tag is dimmed and reads "Matte · nothing behind".
581	
582	On a short row the tag shares the name's line, and it shortens to "Matte" when the name would lose its room.
583	
584	The track's clips are drawn at half opacity with dashed outlines, and a bracket joins the track to the track it cuts. A matte that cuts nothing keeps its dashed outlines and has no bracket.
585	
586	## With an agent
587	
588	`set_track` sets a track's `matte` to `none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#track-mattes). `add_adjustment_clip` adds the adjustment clip, as in [Tools: adding clips](/mcp/tools-adding-clips/#add_adjustment_clip).
589	
590	## Related
591	
592	- [Mattes inside nests](/canvas/mattes-in-nests/)
593	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
594	- [Adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/)
595	- [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/)
596	---
597	title: Mattes inside nests
598	description: See what happens to a matte when you nest or un-nest its tracks, and when a transition crosses them.
599	---
600	
601	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
602	
603	A [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) works inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) the same way it does on the timeline. This page covers what happens where the two meet: a clip inside a nest, nesting and un-nesting matted tracks, and transitions across them.
604	
605	<AtAGlance
606	  menu={['Clip ▸ Nest', 'Clip ▸ Un-nest']}
607	  keys={['⌘G', '⇧⌘G']}
608	  tools={['nest', 'unnest']}
609	/>
610	
611	## Inside a nest
612	
613	With a nest open, **Track ▸ Matte** works on the nest's own tracks, and a matte cuts the track directly behind it among them.
614	
615	A nest clip, the one clip that stands for a nest on the timeline, can also sit on a matte track or on a track a matte cuts:
616	
617	| Where the nest clip sits | What happens |
618	| --- | --- |
619	| On a matte track | Its whole picture is the matte, including any matte inside it. |
620	| On a track cut by a matte | Every layer it draws is cut. At a soft edge, overlapping layers inside the nest show through each other. |
621	
622	A clip inside a nest can come under more than one matte. Frame Job starts at the clip's own track and works outward through each nest around it, out to the timeline:
623	
624	- A matte that cuts a track on the way cuts the clip. With several, the clip shows only where all of them let it through, and at soft edges their strengths multiply.
625	- The first matte track it reaches, whether the clip sits on it or a nest clip around it does, makes the clip part of that matte. Nothing further out applies to it.
626	
627	Two clips showing the same nest at the same moment each have their own matte.
628	
629	Mattes inside nests work with shadows and reflections, at every [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) and in every export.
630	
631	## Nest
632	
633	**Clip ▸ Nest** keeps a track's matte only when the track it cuts is nested with it. Select clips on both tracks and the pair carries into the nest, so the picture stays the same.
634	
635	A matte nested without its target becomes an ordinary track inside the nest. Its clips draw there, so the picture changes unless the nest clip itself lands on a matte track. Undo restores it.
636	
637	The nest clip goes on the front-most of the nested clips' tracks that isn't a matte track, which is where a matte pair's picture was drawn. If every nested clip came from a matte track, it goes on the front-most of them, and the whole nest becomes a matte.
638	
639	## Un-nest
640	
641	**Clip ▸ Un-nest** lines the nest's front-most non-matte track up with the nest clip's track, so the picture comes back as it was. Matte tracks carried in the nest land on the tracks in front of it.
642	
643	Un-nest never makes a track a matte. A carried matte clip is a matte again only if the track it lands on is one, as it is when you un-nest straight after nesting. With no track in front, or no room on it, the clip goes on a new ordinary track in front and draws as an ordinary clip.
644	
645	## Transitions
646	
647	Mattes work through transitions. A dissolve between two clips on a track a matte cuts stays correct under a soft matte, because the same matte cuts both clips.
648	
649	A **Cross Dissolve** or **Zoom** works differently when one of its two clips is a nest clip, or when both clips are inside a nest. Frame Job draws each side whole, with its shadows, reflections and mattes, and then mixes the two pictures, matte or not. That means:
650	
651	- Layers inside one side don't show through each other part-way through.
652	- A matte inside a nest clip is drawn whole, and fades once with its side.
653	- A **Zoom** treats a nest clip as one picture, zooming about the nest clip's centre.
654	- Clips inside the transition draw without [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).
655	
656	Push, slide, wipe and fade transitions aren't mixed this way. They apply to each layer on its own.
657	
658	## Related
659	
660	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
661	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
662	- [Work inside a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/)
663	- [Transition styles](/motion/transition-styles/)
664	- [Show video inside a graphic](/graphics/video-inside-a-graphic/)

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,

  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror

  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of

  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at

  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises

  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11

  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).

  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text

  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of

  where it is (`<package>/graphics`, or an untitled document's

  `packageDidMove(to:)` from the `fileURL` setter, posting
  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its

  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at
  open** (G-14): `ensureFolder()` is the ONE creator inside a package, and
  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).
  `GraphicStore+Files.swift` holds the store's own writes:
  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.

  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.

  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

| <kbd>↓</kbd> | Go to the next edit point. On the last point it stays there. |
| <kbd>Home</kbd> <kbd>End</kbd> | Pause and go to the start or end of the project. The keypad and fn versions of these keys work too. |

An edit point is the start or end of a clip, or either end of the project. <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> beep when there's nothing loaded to play.

<kbd>Space</kbd> does something else in three places:

- In a text field, <kbd>Space</kbd> types a space.
- With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, a focused button, pop-up or segmented control keeps <kbd>Space</kbd> to press itself.
- With the preview canvas focused, a tap of <kbd>Space</kbd> plays or pauses when you release it, because holding it down is how you [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). A <kbd>Space</kbd> held to pan doesn't change playback.

The arrow keys move by word in the [Transcript tab](#transcript-text), and move a selected [curve point](/reference/gestures/#color-tab-controls) in the Color tab.
